scopedFindings: The same launched PID is recorded SIGNALED/status9 at foreground importance100 in all three exit histories; intentional runner cleanup follows death.

Attempts17 and18 record foreground TOP death without matching causal LMKD or ActivityManager kill lines. Their scoped recorders report no gaps or truncation; that scope does not establish absence of an unlogged sender.

Attempt18 kernel console contains no target3282 OOM, seccomp, SELinux, debugger or watchdog cause. Its init SIGKILL messages target other service PIDs; lmkd reinitialization messages do not report an application kill.
The missing36byte process-state summary is length metadata, not decoded sender evidence. Empty crash buffers do not identify the sender.
Elapsed launch-to-death differs across attempts: approximately753seconds,321seconds and61seconds. No one annotation, style/remount or nested-scroll action is established as the shared trigger.

executionChainAudit.result: No demonstrated runner lifetime or explicit application termination route explaining these deaths. Batch row bound2100seconds and inner default3600seconds do not match death times;30second command timers terminate host adb subprocesses. Process-group cleanup operates on owned host processes after failure.

Live markers use react-native-teleport Portal overlays; annotation uses PointAnnotation. Native MainApplication/MainActivity are standard RN templates.
executionChainAudit.limits: Source inspection does not exclude opaque SDK/binary behavior or an external guest sender. No new red-capable native feedback loop ran because native execution is not authorized. A mock injected SIGKILL would not identify the real sender.

offlineCapability.attributionLimit: Raw FtraceEvent.common_pid is execution-context TID. High-level signal slices may discard that context. Queued or kernel-generated signals require care: execution context is not necessarily the original userspace actor; SI_KERNEL does not imply OOM.
